content:
Knowing Our Numbers opens the Class 6 syllabus — Indian and international place value, estimation and Roman numerals carry easy Olympiad marks for a student with the systems straight. Here is what the IMO Class 6 chapter tests, the facts to drill, the slips, and a free 10-question online test from our verified bank.

What the Class 6 Maths Olympiad Knowing Our Numbers chapter tests

  • Indian (lakh/crore) vs international (million) place value
  • Comparing, ordering and building largest/smallest numbers
  • Estimation and rounding to 10, 100, 1000
  • Roman numerals and their rules

Key facts your child should know

  • 1 lakh = 100 thousand; 1 crore = 10 million.
  • Largest number from digits → arrange in descending order (no leading zero for smallest).
  • Round by the next digit — 5 or more rounds up.
  • XL = 40, XC = 90, CM = 900; V, L and D never repeat or subtract.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Mixing lakh-crore commas with million commas.
  • Placing a zero first when building the smallest number.
  • Writing 40 as XXXX instead of XL.

questions.q: In the number 3,70,825, what is the place value of the digit 3 in the lakhs place?
questions.explanation: The digit 3 is in the lakhs place, so its place value = 3 x 1,00,000 = 3,00,000.
Comparing digit by digit from the left, 8,88,880 > 8,88,808.

questions.q: What is the value of the Roman numeral DCCLXXXI?
Which number is represented by "One lakh eighty thousand five hundred"?
What is the smallest 6-digit number that can be formed using the digits 4, 8, 1, 6, 3, 7 (each used once)?
questions.explanation: Arrange digits in ascending order (placing smallest non-zero digit first if 0 is present): 134678 = 1,34,678.

questions.q: Estimate the difference of 9,876 and 4,321 by rounding each to the nearest 1,000.
Find the next number in the pattern: 5, 25, 125, 625, ...
questions.explanation: Following the pattern, the next term is 3125.

faq.q: What is the difference between lakh and million?
faq.a: One lakh is 100,000 (1,00,000 in Indian commas); one million is 1,000,000 — so 10 lakh = 1 million.

faq.q: What are the rules for Roman numerals?
faq.a: A smaller symbol before a bigger one subtracts (XL = 40); a symbol repeats at most three times; V, L and D never repeat or subtract.
